title: Glucose and ketone readings
summary: Finger-prick meter readings, logged from a photo of the meter.
description: People on a ketogenic diet or a long fast watch blood glucose and ketones, and above all their ratio. A photo of the meter's screen is enough to log one.

requirements.text: Glucose is shown in one unit for every reading: the unit of the last meter photo that showed one, mmol/L until then.

history.text: Glucose is shown in the unit the meter showed it in (mmol/L or mg/dL).
history.reason: Version 1 said each reading keeps its meter's unit; the unit is a single setting applied to all readings.

requirements.text: A glucose and a ketone reading taken within `reading.pair-window` of each other, with ketones above zero, show their glucose–ketone index (glucose ÷ ketones).

history.text: A glucose and a ketone reading taken within `reading.pair-window` of each other show their glucose–ketone index (glucose ÷ ketones).
history.reason: No index is shown when ketones read zero.

requirements.text: A reading outside `reading.glucose-range` (glucose) or `reading.ketone-range` (ketones) is rejected and not stored.

history.text: A reading outside the meter's measurable range is treated as a misread, not stored as given.
history.reason: Version 1 was vague about what happens to an out-of-range reading and didn't name the ranges.

requirements.text: A reading's page shows a trend of the 30 days up to that reading's day, when at least two of those days have readings.

history.text: A reading's page shows a 30-day trend.
history.reason: The trend ends on the reading's day and is hidden with fewer than two days of readings.
